question: Top 5 potato-eating countries
stat_label: Potatoes available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Belarus (166.9 kg), Ukraine (147.0), Bosnia and Herzegovina (102.9), Nepal (99.5) and Kyrgyzstan (98.8) make the top 5. Poland just misses at #6 (92.9 kg), and Ireland is #10 (85.3 kg).
headline: Potato-eaters

question: Top 5 wine-drinking countries
stat_label: Wine available for consumption per person, FAO food balance
source_name: UN FAO Food Balances via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Luxembourg (75.9 kg), Portugal (53.5), Belgium (48.0), France (45.7) and Italy (37.7) make the top 5. Switzerland is #6 (31.8 kg), Spain only #16 (18.2) and Georgia #43 (9.5).
headline: Wine O'Clock

question: Top 5 tea-drinking countries
stat_label: Tea consumption per capita (kg per year)
source_name: Statista (2016, paywalled; original publisher unverified) via Wikipedia "List of countries by tea consumption per capita" (revision of 10 Feb 2020)
fun_fact: Top 5: Turkey, Ireland, UK, Russia, Morocco. China (#18) and India (#26) are nowhere near. Caveat: Statista (2016) via Wikipedia; it covers only 53 countries and the original methodology isn't public.
headline: Tea Time

question: Top 5 carbon footprints
stat_label: Consumption-based CO₂ per person (Global Carbon Project)
source_name: Global Carbon Budget via Our World in Data
fun_fact: Singapore leads with 32.3 t per person, ahead of Qatar (27.6) and Malta (26.8). The US is #11 (15.8), China #36 (7.6) and the UK #41 (7.1).
headline: Carbon Footprints

question: Where men grew taller, 1985–2019
stat_label: Change in mean height of 19-year-old boys, 1985 to 2019
fun_fact: China: its 19-year-old men gained 8.0 cm (167.6 to 175.7 cm), more than anywhere else. Saudi Arabia (+7.7) and South Korea and the Maldives (+6.8 each) follow. US men gained only 1.2 cm.
headline: Growth Spurt

question: Top 5 K-pop-searching countries
stat_label: Google search interest in K-pop (music genre topic)
source_name: Google Trends, interest by region (country), past 5 years, topic entity, fetched 20 Oct 2026
fun_fact: The Philippines Googles K-pop more than anywhere, ahead of Singapore and Myanmar. South Korea itself is only #5. South Korea and Indonesia tie at #5 (51), so either counts. Caveat: Google Trends measures each country's share of its own Google searches over the past 5 years (scaled so the top country = 100), not search volume or fans. Countries with little Google use are left out.
headline: Stan Nations

question: Top 5 alcohol-drinking countries
stat_label: Total alcohol per capita (age 15+), litres of pure alcohol, 2020
source_name: World Bank / WHO: Total alcohol consumption per capita (SH.ALC.PCAP.LI)
fun_fact: Romania (16.8 L), Georgia (14.41), Latvia (12.87), Lithuania (12.1) and Czechia (11.99) make the top 5 (litres of pure alcohol per adult, 2020). Germany just misses at #6 (11.84 L).
headline: Top Shelf

question: Where 19-year-old women grew taller, 1985–2019
stat_label: Change in mean height of 19-year-old girls, 1985 to 2019
fun_fact: Saudi Arabia: its 19-year-old women gained 6.2 cm (152.6 to 158.8 cm), more than anywhere else. South Korea and China gained 6.1 cm each, then Turkey (+5.7) and Vietnam (+5.4). US women gained only 0.4 cm.
headline: She Grew

question: Transgender, non-binary, gender-fluid or other (online survey of adults)
source_name: Ipsos LGBT+ Pride 2023 Global Survey (30 countries; online adults, mostly 16-74, fieldwork 17 Feb–3 Mar 2023), gender identity by country: net of transgender, non-binary/gender non-conforming/gender-fluid, or other than male or female
fun_fact: Switzerland leads at 6% and Thailand is next at 5%. The United States is tied for 15th of 30 at 2%. Thailand's sample is more urban and educated than the country. Note: Ipsos online survey of adults, 2023. Across the 30 countries, 6% of Gen Z identify this way versus 1% of Boomers. Spain is also 4%, tied with Italy, Sweden and Germany.
headline: Counted In
